neighbours.label: ' a', ' an' or ' your' right after an imperative to consult someone (Ask a, Talk to your, Consult a, See your), firing on the determiner; the same determiners after verbs of reading, buying or making stay low
fire: If the rash gets worse, ask a pharmacist for advice.
Questions about tax? Ask an Accountant on our forum.
Before changing your diet, talk to your nurse.
Still confused? Speak to your supervisor this week.
Please consult a surveyor before you buy the land.
For back pain, see your physician without delay.
Unsure about the will? Consult an attorney first.
Our site lets you Ask a Vet for free.
